identity.title: An Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Survey of Chemistry in Disks around M4-M5 Stars

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present an ALMA survey of molecular line emission toward a sample of five protoplanetary disks around M4-M5 stars (FP Tau, J0432+1827, J1100-7619, J1545-3417, and Sz 69).

In this study, we present an Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) exploratory survey of molecules toward a sample of five disks around M4-M5 stars, and we draw preliminary conclusions on chemistry across the disks.

question.value: What is the chemistry of protoplanetary disks around low-mass M4-M5 stars at 10-100 AU scales, and how does it compare to disks around solar-type stars?

evidence.quote: We present an ALMA survey of molecular line emission toward a sample of five protoplanetary disks around M4-M5 stars (FP Tau, J0432+1827, J1100-7619, J1545-3417, and Sz 69).
Overall, most of the observable chemistry at 10-100AU appears similar for solar-type and M4-M5 disks, but hydrocarbons may be more abundant around the cooler stars.
To date, disk chemistry around low-mass M-stars (stellar masses $<$0.5M$_\Sun$, spectral types typically from $\sim$M4-M9) has barely been explored beyond the inner $\sim$10 AU.
All five disks were observed with ALMA during Project 2017.1.01107.S from December 2017 through September 2018.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.01107.S.
We survey the overall chemistry of these disks by targeting 1.1mm and 1.3mm lines of CO isotopologues and precursor organic molecules.
Total and peak emission for the 1.1mm (262GHz) and 1.3mm (231GHz) dust continuum were measured within the bounds of the $^{12}$CO and HCN Keplerian masks, respectively

self_calibration.value: Line-free continuum combined from all spws; Briggs robust=0.5; 2 rounds phase and 1 round amplitude when able; solint 10-100s (J1545-3417, Sz 69), 70-210s (FP Tau), none for J0432+1827 and J1100-7619

evidence.quote: We self-calibrated each observation using the line-free continuum combined from all spectral windows. We uniformly used Briggs weighting and a robust value of 0.5. We performed two rounds of phase calibration and one round of amplitude calibration per observation when able.
Solution intervals for the disks J1545-3417 and Sz 69 ranged from 10-100 seconds for each observation.
Due to low continuum fluxes, we used solution intervals from 70-210 seconds for the five observations toward FP Tau. We were unable to self-calibrate on the continuum for J0432+1827 and J1100-7619.
We used `CASA`’s `uvcontsub` and `clean` functions to (1) subtract the continuum from each spectral window and (2) image each molecular line.
In order to balance sensitivity and resolution, we imaged each line using Briggs weighting and a robust value of 0.5.

We imaged the dust continuum and molecular line emission toward the disk observed with the highest resolution (J1100-7619) with a pixel size of 0.02", while we imaged the emission toward the other four disks in the sample (FP Tau, J0432+1827, J1545-3417, and Sz 69) with a pixel size of 0.04".

masking.value: Hand-drawn masks per channel (cleaned to 2 sigma for bright lines); recycled masks from brighter lines for fainter lines (cleaned to 3 sigma)

evidence.quote: We created `clean`ing masks by hand to cover the molecular emission and little else in each channel. For fainter lines, we recycled `clean`ing masks from brighter lines and `clean`ed down to 3$\sigma$ rather than the deeper 2$\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is the average rms across non-emission channels, to avoid creating image artifacts.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate disk centers and extract line/continuum emission with Keplerian masks

method.value: Fit 2D Gaussians to the dust continuum to find disk centers; apply Keplerian masks across emission velocity channels to extract spectra, moment 0 maps, radial profiles, and integrated fluxes; estimate uncertainties via 1000 random/bootstrapped samples.

evidence.quote: We estimated the disk centers using two-dimensional Gaussian fits to the dust continuum emission. We used Keplerian masks (cite: cite_rosenfeldetal2013a; cite_yenetal2016; cite_salinasetal2017) to extract emission for each disk (cite: cite_kepmask) across all emission channels for each molecular line.
We used the Keplerian-masked channels to then generate spectra, velocity-integrated emission maps, radial profiles, and integrated fluxes.

We took the average rms across 1000 $2"\times2"$ random samples of non-emission channels to be the channel rms. We estimated the noise for the integrated fluxes via bootstrapping over 1000 Keplerian-masked random samples of non-emission channels.

Changes in optical depth from 4 to 12 lead to factors $\lesssim$3 in difference between estimates, while changes in excitation temperature from 10K to 30K lead to factors of $\sim$3-10 (excluding Sz 69).

results_numeric.quantity: J1100-7619 disk-averaged median DCN column density

evidence.quote: For the bright and well-resolved disk J1100-7619, DCN is detected, and the estimated column densities (not shown) span $\sim$(4-10)$\times 10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$ from 10-30K with a median of $\sim$7$\times 10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Disk-averaged median C2H/HCN column density ratio across M4-M5 sample

evidence.quote: Median estimates of the ratio range from $\sim$7 for FP Tau to $\sim$11 for J1545-3417.

results_numeric.quantity: J1100-7619 disk-averaged median DCN/HCN column density ratio

evidence.quote: This disk has a median DCN/HCN value of $\sim$0.072 and ranges from $\sim$0.04-0.1 across the extremes.

findings_qualitative.value: 12CO, 13CO, C18O, C2H, and HCN are detected toward all 5 M4-M5 disks; H2CO is detected toward 2/5 (and tentatively 2/5); DCN is detected toward 1/5 (and tentatively 4/5).

evidence.quote: 1. We detect $^{12}$CO 2–1, $^{13}$CO 2–1, C$^{18}$O 2–1, C$_2$H 3–2, and HCN 3–2 toward 5/5 disks. We detect H$_2$CO 3–2 toward 2/5 disks and tentatively detect it toward two other disks. We detect DCN 3–2 toward 1/5 disks and tentatively detect it toward all other disks (see Section 4.1).

findings_qualitative.value: Dust continuum emission is smooth across all 5 disks at 0.12-0.29" resolution, while CO isotopologues are centrally peaked and well-resolved C2H, HCN, and H2CO show substructures (holes, rings, plateaus) similar to solar-type disks.

evidence.quote: For disks with resolved C$^{18}$O, C$_2$H, HCN, and H$_2$CO emission, we observe substructures similar to those previously found in disks around solar-type stars (e.g., rings, holes, and plateaus).
2. The dust continuum emission toward all five disks in the sample is smooth at this resolution (0.12-0.29").

findings_qualitative.value: C2H and HCN fluxes are strongly correlated in M4-M5 disks as in solar-type disks, but M4-M5 disks have higher C2H/HCN flux and column density ratios than solar-type disks, indicating enhanced hydrocarbon abundance.

evidence.quote: The correlation previously found between C$_2$H and HCN fluxes for solar-type disks extends to our M4-M5 disk sample, but the typical C$_2$H/HCN ratio is higher for the M4-M5 disk sample.

findings_qualitative.value: In J1100-7619, radial C2H and HCN column density profiles differ interior to the pebble disk edge (HCN drops steeply while C2H is flat), whereas their flux ratio is constant beyond the pebble disk edge, suggesting coupled chemistry in the outer disk.

evidence.quote: It is important to note how the C$_2$H and HCN column density profiles measured across the pebble disk for J1100-7619 (Figure 9) are different in shape, with the HCN column densities decreasing more steeply across the pebble disk than the C$_2$H column densities.
(C$_2$H 3–2 / HCN 3–2) increases with radius across the pebble disk, and then is constant beyond the pebble disk edge (see Section 4.4.1).

claims.hypothesis: Observable outer-disk (10-100 AU) chemistry and molecular emission substructures around low-mass M4-M5 stars share similar underlying physical/chemical processes to disks around solar-type stars.
claims.experiment: Observed 12CO, 13CO, C18O, C2H, HCN, DCN, and H2CO lines with ALMA toward 5 M4-M5 disks, analyzed emission morphologies and flux correlations, and performed pixel-by-pixel hyperfine fits on J1100-7619 to compare with solar-type literature samples.
claims.result: Substructures (rings, holes, plateaus) are seen in resolved C2H, HCN, and H2CO; C2H and HCN fluxes are strongly correlated (r = 0.92 combined, r = 1.00 M4-M5); J1100-7619 C2H and HCN T_ex (10-25 K) and optical depths match solar-type disks; line flux ratios show no trend with stellar mass.
claims.finding: Most observable chemistry at 10-100 AU is similar between M4-M5 and solar-type disks, implying similar underlying physical and chemical processes.

evidence.quote: For disks with resolved C$^{18}$O, C$_2$H, HCN, and H$_2$CO emission, we observe substructures similar to those previously found in disks around solar-type stars (e.g., rings, holes, and plateaus).
Overall, most of the observable chemistry at 10-100AU appears similar for solar-type and M4-M5 disks, but hydrocarbons may be more abundant around the cooler stars.

These results imply similar underlying physical/chemical processes for the M4-M5 disks and the solar-type disks, consistent with the predictions for brown dwarf disks relative to T Tauri disks from thermochemical modeling (cite: cite_greenwoodetal2017).

claims.hypothesis: Hydrocarbon chemistry (C2H relative to HCN) is enhanced in the outer regions of disks around cooler M4-M5 stars compared to solar-type stars, analogous to inner-disk (<10 AU) infrared C2H2/HCN enhancements.
claims.experiment: Measured disk-integrated C2H 3-2 / HCN 3-2 flux ratios and derived disk-averaged C2H/HCN column density ratios for the 5 M4-M5 disks, comparing them against the 16th, 50th, and 84th percentiles of solar-type disks.
claims.result: M4-M5 disk-averaged C2H/HCN column density ratios have medians of 7 to 11, all exceeding the 84th percentile (4.7) of the solar-type disk sample, and C2H/HCN flux ratios are similarly elevated.
claims.finding: Hydrocarbon production relative to HCN is enhanced in the outer disks around M4-M5 stars compared to solar-type stars, though a larger unbiased sample is needed to confirm.

evidence.quote: Median estimates of the ratio range from $\sim$7 for FP Tau to $\sim$11 for J1545-3417. Notably all C$_2$H/HCN estimates for the M4-M5 disks exceed the 84$^\mathrm{th}$ percentile of the solar-type and Herbig Ae disk C$_2$H/HCN estimates.

The C$_2$H 3–2 / HCN 3–2 flux ratios are also higher for the M4-M5 disks compared to the solar-type disks. These enhancements imply greater hydrocarbon production in the M4-M5 disks relative to the solar-type disks.

claims.hypothesis: The strong correlation between C2H 3-2 and HCN 3-2 fluxes is driven by shared outer-disk physical/chemical drivers rather than simply being an artifact of both lines being optically thick.
claims.experiment: Compared C2H 3-2 and HCN 3-2 integrated fluxes against optically thick 13CO 2-1 fluxes across the M4-M5 sample, and examined radial profiles of column density and flux ratios in J1100-7619.
claims.result: Neither C2H nor HCN shows the same variation with 13CO 2-1 as they do with each other; in J1100-7619, C2H/HCN flux ratio is constant (~0.8-0.9) beyond the pebble disk edge (~100 AU) while their inner-disk column density profiles diverge.
claims.finding: Optical depth alone cannot explain the C2H-HCN correlation; C2H and HCN likely share common physical/chemical drivers beyond the pebble disk edge while being decoupled interior to it.

evidence.quote: This further suggests that the similarities and correlations between C$_2$H and HCN morphologies, fluxes, and disk-averaged column densities discussed here are driven by the emission *beyond* the pebble disk.

evidence.loc: Investigation of Optical Depth as the Primary Contributor to Flux Correlations
evidence.quote: However, we see that neither C$_2$H 3–2 nor HCN 3–2 show the same variation with $^{13}$CO 2–1. This is evidence against a shared dependence of the relative line fluxes on optical depth. We thus conclude that optically thick emission is not the primary reason for the C$_2$H 3–2 vs. HCN 3–2 correlation we find in Section 4.3.

claims.hypothesis: H2CO and C2H formation in the outer disk are linked via UV photodesorption of CO ice beyond the pebble disk edge rather than thermal CO freeze-out at the CO snowline.
claims.experiment: Compared radial emission profiles of H2CO 3-2 and C2H 3-2 in J1100-7619 and estimated the midplane CO snowline radius using a power-law temperature profile.
claims.result: In J1100-7619, H2CO rings at ~60 AU and ~150 AU align with the C2H peak and outer bump near/beyond the pebble disk edge, whereas the estimated CO snowline upper limit is interior at ~22-43 AU.
claims.finding: The spatial alignment of H2CO and C2H features exterior to the CO snowline and pebble disk edge points to a linked dependence on UV photodesorption of CO ice.

evidence.quote: The first ring in H$_2$CO emission toward this disk is roughly aligned with the peak in the C$_2$H emission at $\sim$60AU, and both peaks are located near the edge of the pebble disk. The second ring in H$_2$CO emission is roughly aligned with a small bump in the C$_2$H emission at $\sim$150AU.

assuming a simple radial temperature profile with a power law exponent of 0.55, a temperature of 142K at 1 AU (cite: cite_andrewsetal2007), and CO midplane freeze-out temperatures of 18-26K (cite: cite_obergetal2011b), we estimate upper limits on the CO snowline of $\sim$22-43 AU, which are interior to both H$_2$CO peaks.
Similar radial substructure of the H$_2$CO and C$_2$H emission may point to a linked dependence on the UV photodesorption of CO ice beyond the pebble disk (see Sections 5.1 and 5.2).

why_this_data.value: Five M4-M5 disks from multiple star-forming regions (Taurus, Lupus, Chamaeleon I) were selected for bright 12CO and 13CO detections in existing ALMA surveys to avoid single-cloud bias and match selection criteria of early solar-type disk chemistry surveys.

evidence.quote: The disks were chosen from multiple star-forming regions, avoiding bias toward any one molecular cloud.

We note that the five disks in the M4-M5 disk sample were selected specifically for their bright $^{12}$CO (J=3–2) and $^{13}$CO (J=3–2) detections in existing ALMA disk surveys (cite: cite_ansdelletal2016; cite_longetal2017). These selection criteria are similar to those used by early exploratory chemistry surveys of solar-type and Herbig Ae disks

why_this_method.value: Keplerian masks reduce noise in integrated emission; pixel-by-pixel hyperfine fitting reduces line blending and avoids systematic errors from radial variations in line width, center, and peak.

evidence.quote: Keplerian masks decrease the amount of noise that is incorporated into the integrated emission.

By fitting to the spectrum through each pixel, we reduce line blending of the hyperfine components of the spectra, which allows for tighter constraints on the fit. We also avoid systematic errors due to changes in line width, line center, and line peak as a function of disk location.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Optical depth as the primary driver of the C2H vs. HCN flux correlation was investigated by comparing against optically thick 13CO 2-1 fluxes and rejected.

evidence.loc: Investigation of Optical Depth as the Primary Contributor to Flux Correlations
evidence.quote: We thus conclude that optically thick emission is not the primary reason for the C$_2$H 3–2 vs. HCN 3–2 correlation we find in Section 4.3.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Planck-correcting the background continuum temperature prior to calculating excitation temperature (used in previous studies) was rejected as an over-correction.

evidence.quote: Note that unlike the previous studies, we do not calculate the Planck-corrected temperature of the background continuum prior to Equation [\[eq_Texset_Tex1\]](#eq_Texset_Tex1), as this is an over-correction of the background brightness temperature.

limitations_admitted.value: Sample size is small (5 disks) and biased toward bright, gas-rich M4-M5 disks.

evidence.quote: We stress that our sample is biased toward bright, gas-rich M4-M5 disks, and that these findings serve as an *initial* window into $>$10AU disk chemistry for low-mass M-stars.

limitations_admitted.value: Significant cloud contamination affects CO emission in 3/5 disks (FP Tau, J1545-3417, and Sz 69).

evidence.quote: The disks FP Tau, J1545-3417, and Sz 69 are significantly affected by cloud contamination, which is evident in the CO spectra and the CO channel maps (Appendix 10).

limitations_admitted.value: Pixel-by-pixel hyperfine fits have significant intrinsic uncertainties (up to ~40% at high optical depths) due to narrow line widths (0.2-0.5 km/s) vs. coarse velocity resolution (0.14 km/s), unmodeled pixel-to-pixel correlations, reliance on faint HCN satellite lines, and breakdown of Gaussian line shape assumptions at high optical depth.

evidence.quote: First, the C$_2$H and HCN pixel-by-pixel spectra toward J1100-7619 have relatively small line widths ($\sim$0.2-0.5km s$^{-1}$) because of the disk’s low inclination angle. This fact, coupled with the relatively coarse velocity resolution of the data (0.14km s$^{-1}$), means that the hyperfine procedure has a limited number of data points to fit for each hyperfine component.
Second, the pixel-by-pixel fitting procedure does not account for uncertainties due to correlations between neighboring pixels. Third, the error in the fits is intrinsically large.
At the optical depths we are encountering for C$_2$H and HCN, uncertainties intrinsic to the model may become as large as $\sim$40%.

limitations_admitted.value: Literature distances were used instead of updated Gaia DR2 distances to maintain consistency with literature stellar characteristics (which changes J1100-7619 distance from 160 pc to 191.5 pc).

evidence.quote: The distances in parentheses are the distances assumed in the literature for these disks. We use the values in parentheses throughout this paper to be consistent with the derived stellar characteristics.

referee_caveats_inferred: Using literature distance (160 pc) rather than the Gaia distance (191.5 pc) for J1100-7619 underestimates its physical radii by ~20% and luminosity/distance-normalized fluxes by ~43%.
Two disks (J0432+1827 and J1100-7619) could not be self-calibrated while the other three were self-calibrated, introducing inhomogeneous phase/amplitude calibration across the sample.
